one_month_reasoning: No earnings in the window: Q4 2026 results and the first FY2027 guide come around 2027-01-20, after 2026-12-17. In-window events are the Thanksgiving Eve NFL game (2026-11-25) and the build-up to the Christmas doubleheader (src 25). Both are ad-sales tests already in the ~$2.7B guide, so they should not move the stock much. The stock is at its 52-week low after a 46% fall. Momentum and short-term reversal pull in opposite directions, and the alternative data has no dated print in the window. So the ladder is near-symmetric lognormal around a median of $59.50 at monthly volatility 36%/3.5 = 10.3%.

fair_value.method: Quarterly driver build (memberships x subscription ARM + ad revenue, less content cost and opex) gives NTM GAAP EPS of about $4.18 at 2027-11-17. Valued at a 16.59x P/E: the whole-company peer median of 17.66x shrunk toward Netflix's own 16.33x with k = 0.8. Result $69.32.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM (Nov-2027 to Nov-2028) GAAP EPS ~$4.18 from the driver build (FY2027 revenue $55.7B +9.0%, margin 33.0%; FY2028 $60.3B, 34.1%; shares -4%/yr) x 16.59x

inputs_detail.derivation: Actual-quarter values are estimates (Netflix stopped reporting memberships in 2025): 2025 path 308/313/318/325 joins the reported 301.63M (Q4 2024) to the stated >325M (Q4 2025). 2026: +15M (4.6%) to 340M: Q1-Q3 2026 revenue grew 16%/13%/12% reported (11% FX-neutral in Q3) while the US price rise of Mar-2026 (ads $7.99->$8.99, Standard $17.99->$19.99, src 22) and UCAN +11% (src 4) leave little room for US volume, so most adds are international. 2027: +12M (3.5%) to 352M, with +3.5M in Q2 for the ad-tier launch in 12 countries in March 2027 (src 4, 21); 2028: +10M (2.8%). Alternative-data read: Apptopia shows US non-openers +16.6% y/y in Q3 2026 (src 13), Nielsen has Netflix at 7.7% of US TV vs YouTube 15.8% (src 14, 15), H1 2026 view hours only +2% (src 5): all point to saturating volume, hence the deceleration.
inputs_detail.variant_view: If the Apptopia and Nielsen engagement slide (src 13, 14) turns into churn, 2027 adds could halve to ~6M: revenue -1.5% by FY2028 and the research target (12m) -6.2% (engine: 65.00 vs 69.32).

inputs_detail.value: FY2025 ~$11.62, FY2026 ~$12.15, FY2027 +3.0%, FY2028 +3.5% (quarter values in drivers)
inputs_detail.derivation: Actual quarters are the residual that reproduces filed revenue (src 3) given the members and ad_rev estimates. Q4 2026 $12.415 (+1.9% q/q) gives revenue $13,419M, 0.2% under the $13,442M guide (src 4) for the stronger dollar since the guide (DXY at a 19-month high, src 26) and the record of near-zero recent revenue beats (guidance_check). 2027: +3.0% y/y per quarter: no US price step is due until about two years after Mar-2026 (prior US steps Jan-2025 and Mar-2026, src 22), international price rounds continue (Mexico, Spain in H1 2026, src 5, 6), and the March 2027 ad-tier launch in 15 lower-ARM markets dilutes mix. 2028: +3.5% with a likely next US price step. Alternatives: (a) 2026 realized ARM growth (~+4.5% Q4/Q4) held; (b) +2% if price rises meet the churn that the engagement data warns of (src 13, 19).
inputs_detail.variant_view: +2% ARM growth (price rises meet churn): target -6.3% (engine 64.95); +4.5% (2026 pace): +6.6% (73.89).

inputs_detail.derivation: Quarter split of 2025 ($1.5B) and 2026 ($2.7B) is an estimate weighted to Q4 (NFL Christmas games, holiday CPMs; Thanksgiving Eve and Christmas games in 2026, src 25). 2027 = +40% ($3.78B): ad-tier monthly active viewers 250M+ at the May 2026 upfront (src 21) growing ~15-20% with 15 launch markets, plus ~20% yield from programmatic and the in-house ad suite; 2028 +28% ($4.84B). Alternatives: Omdia $8B by 2030 (~31%/yr from $2.7B, src 20, stale and reconciled); the Oct-2026 rollout delay (src 4) repeating, -25%.
inputs_detail.variant_view: Another rollout slip (-25% on 2027-28 ads): target -6.1% (engine 65.10).

inputs_detail.derivation: Q4 2026 $7,100M = Q4 2025 $6,522.6M (src 3) x 1.089, the 9M-2026 content amortization growth (+9.5%, src 4) less a small step for the Q3 expense-timing shift the letter names (src 4); it gives Q4 operating income $3,479M vs the $3,500M guide. 2027 +7.5% and 2028 +6.5% y/y: cash content spend stays ~1.1x amortization (src 4, 7), the new content leadership is tasked with hit rate, not volume (src 19 relays BofA), and the 6% headcount cut (src 4) points to cost discipline. Alternative: +10% a year (2026 pace) as Netflix spends to answer the engagement slide (src 13, 14), -1.2pt margin.
inputs_detail.variant_view: +10% a year (content push to defend engagement): target -7.7% (engine 64.00).

inputs_detail.derivation: Q4 2026 $2,840M includes ~$160M of severance (~120bp of Q4 revenue, src 4); this sets Q4 operating margin at 25.9% vs the 26.0% guide. 2027 $10,336M = 2026 ex severance ($9,751M) +6%: the ~1,000-role cut saves cost (src 4) but ad-tier launches in 15 markets and the ad-tech build add marketing and engineering; 2028 +6%. Alternative: +9% (2025-26 pace ex severance) costs ~0.5pt of margin.

inputs_detail.derivation: Cost of net debt: TTM interest expense 856.9 (F74) / gross debt 15,132.4 (F96) = 5.66%; new debt prices off a 10-year Treasury above 5% (src 26), so 5.8% on incremental net debt.

anchor.note: content cash spend ~1.1x amortization; gap modelled in other_uses

inputs_detail.derivation: Cash content spend ~1.1x amortization (src 4, 7): amortization ~70% of cost of revenues (9M 2026 $12.76B of $18.0B, src 4) -> ~$17.5-20B a year, x 0.1 = $1.7-2.0B of cash content in excess of the P&L charge, plus the Q4 2026 real-estate purchase in the FY2026 FCF guide.

inputs_detail.derivation: Q3 2026 weighted diluted shares (F33).
Debt 15,132.4 - cash 8,194.3 - short-term investments 28.7 (F97); the letter's $7.1B counts debt at $15.3B face.

Whole-company peers DIS 15.5x (DIS.pe_ntm), SONY 17.66x, SPOT 38.86x (peers.md refresh) -> median 17.66x. Own NTM P/E 16.33x (price 59.68 / NTM consensus EPS 3.655, peers.md; we checked the Zacks quarters: Q4-26 0.67, 2027 0.92/0.96/1.00/0.86, src 9). Exit = 17.66 x (16.33/17.66)^0.8 = 16.59x (k = 0.8 default). Alternatives: the run's booked 16.83x (META/GOOGL median, src 12) +1.4%; DIS alone (15.5x) -7%; Netflix's own NTM 16.33x held -1.6%.
inputs_detail.variant_view: A media-style de-rating to DIS's 15.5x takes the target about -7%; a return of the growth premium (~20x) +20%.

downside.story: P10: the engagement slide in the alternative data (Apptopia non-openers +16.6%, Nielsen share stuck at 7.7% vs YouTube's 15.8%, top-original hours -21% per Wells Fargo) turns into churn and price resistance: ~8M fewer members, ARM 3% lower, ads 25% below plan after another rollout slip, and a content push that lifts cost of revenues 2.5%. FY2027 revenue growth drops to ~5% and margins stall near 30%; the market prices Netflix like legacy media (~13.6x NTM, below DIS).

base.story: Median: memberships +3.5%/+2.8% in 2027/28, ARM +3.0%/+3.5%, ads $3.8B/$4.8B, content cost +7.5%/+6.5%. Revenue +9.0% in FY2027 (1.7% under the $56.67B consensus), operating margin 33.0% then 34.1%, buybacks retiring ~4% of shares a year. EPS ~$3.7 in FY2027 (consensus $3.74) and ~$4.3 in FY2028 (consensus $4.43) at 16.6x NTM.

upside.story: P90: the new content leadership lands hits, the 15-country ad launch and ad suite take ads toward $4.7B in 2027, a 2027 US price step sticks with churn still the lowest in the industry (Antenna), and margins pass 35% in 2028; the growth premium partly returns (~20.6x NTM).

thesis_triggers.event: Q4 2026 revenue below the $13.44B guide, or a FY2027 revenue guide under +9% in January
thesis_triggers.check: The 2027-01 letter's FY2027 revenue range and Q1 2027 forecast against our $55.7B (+9.0%); a guide midpoint under ~$55B breaks the member and ARM path.

thesis_triggers.event: Engagement slide becomes measurable churn: Antenna monthly churn rising well above ~2%, or the Nielsen Gauge share falling under 7% for two months
thesis_triggers.check: Antenna releases and Nielsen The Gauge monthly; Apptopia app-open data; Netflix's semiannual engagement report (H2 2026 hours vs +2% in H1).

thesis_triggers.event: Another ad roadmap slip: the March 2027 ad-tier launch in 12 countries delayed, or 2027 ad revenue guided under ~$3.5B
thesis_triggers.check: Q4 2026 letter and the May 2027 upfront (monthly active ad viewers vs 250M+), ad-suite partner announcements.

thesis_triggers.event: Content cost reset: the new content leadership raises spend (cash content over 1.2x amortization) or Netflix bids for a large sports or studio asset
thesis_triggers.check: Cash flow statement content additions vs amortization each 10-Q; any rights deal or M&A 8-K; FY2027 FCF guide well under ~$12B.

key_uncertainties: Membership growth: no longer disclosed, so our path rests on alternative data and revenue arithmetic.
Whether falling per-member engagement (Apptopia, Nielsen, Wells Fargo) turns into churn or only weakens pricing power.
Ad monetization after the 2026 rollout delay.
Content spend direction under the new content leadership.
FX: a strong dollar (DXY at a 19-month high) weighs on reported ARM.

long_dated_risks.risk: YouTube and creator video keep taking TV share (15.8% vs Netflix 7.7% of US TV) and cap Netflix's pricing power after 2028
long_dated_risks.cash_flow_effect: Post-2028 revenue growth ~5% instead of ~8% and margins plateau near 34%; NTM EPS growth at the horizon falls from ~15% to ~9%

long_dated_risks.risk: Paramount-WBD combination (HBO Max + Paramount+) bundles a larger rival library and bids up talent and sports costs
long_dated_risks.cash_flow_effect: Content cost growth +1-2pt a year above our path after the deal closes; ~1pt margin

reverse_dcf_check: 16.59x NTM GAAP earnings with net debt near 1x EBITDA implies about a 6% earnings yield. At a ~10% cost of equity that means long-run earnings growth of about 4-5% a year after 2028: revenue growth fading from ~8% to mid-single digits with margins held near 34%. That is plausible for a maturing subscription leader facing YouTube for share.

sbc_treatment.note: GAAP operating income and EPS already include SBC (FY2025 $368.4M, F43; TTM $540.1M, F46), so it is not added back. The share count falls only by net buybacks (-4%/yr), and peer P/Es are on GAAP/consensus EPS after SBC.

reasoning: Start: the stock is at $59.68, down 46% in a year, at 16.3x NTM consensus EPS. The fall followed three things: revenue growth slowing each quarter (16% -> 13% -> 12% -> ~11.5% guided for Q4), the cut to the 2026 ad target ($3.0B -> $2.7B), and evidence of weaker engagement. Lane work (alternative data) tested whether the engagement worry is real. It is, but it shows up mostly in volume, not yet in churn. Apptopia (via Bloomberg/A.V. Club) has US subscribers not opening the app up 16.6% y/y in Q3. Nielsen's Gauge (TheWrap, Tubefilter) puts Netflix at 7.7% of US TV against YouTube's record 15.8%. The Entertainment Strategy Guy and Hub Intel Substack show returning shows losing audiences and per-user viewing falling. Stocktwits retail sentiment is extremely bearish. On the other side, Antenna data still shows strong Premium uptake among cord-cutters, and the company says price rises in the US, Mexico and Spain went as expected. My read: pricing still works but member growth is saturating, so the base case decelerates memberships (+4.6% in 2026, +3.5%, +2.8%) and keeps ARM at +3-3.5%, below the 2026 pace. Ads come from company statements (250M+ monthly active ad viewers, 15 new markets in 2027), not the stale Omdia path, which I reconciled. Guidance record: quarterly revenue beats have shrunk to about zero in 2026 and margin beats came from expense timing, so Q4 sits just under the guide. Content cost (+7.5%/+6.5%) and opex give 33.0%/34.1% margins. EPS ends 2-3% under consensus. Valuation follows the playbook: P/E on our own GAAP EPS with the k = 0.8 shrink toward a thin 3-name whole-company peer median (17.66x), giving 16.59x and $69.32 (+16%). That is mostly buyback-driven EPS growth at a flat multiple. Downside (P10, $42.24) has the engagement slide turning into churn, an ad slip, a content push and a de-rating to ~13.6x. Upside (P90, $102.86) has ads and pricing working and a partial return of the premium. Engine-sized judgment calls over 5% are listed in gap_note for Kilian. Research used about 25 searches and fetches; X/Twitter, Reddit and several data-vendor pages (Apptopia, MediaPost/Antenna, Puck, eMarketer, MarketBeat) blocked fetching, so I relied on reachable relays of them and flagged each relay. No option prices were consulted.

downside.story: P10: the engagement slide in the alternative data (Apptopia non-openers +16.6%, Nielsen share stuck at 7.7% vs YouTube's 15.8%, top-original hours -21% per Wells Fargo) turns into churn and price resistance: ~8M fewer members, ARM 3% lower, ads 25% below plan after another rollout slip, and a content push that lifts cost of revenues 2.5%. FY2027 revenue growth drops to ~5% and margins stall near 30%; the market prices Netflix like legacy media (~13.6x NTM, below DIS).

upside.story: P90: the new content leadership lands hits, the 15-country ad launch and ad suite take ads toward $4.7B in 2027, a 2027 US price step sticks with churn still the lowest in the industry (Antenna), and margins pass 35% in 2028; the growth premium partly returns (~20.6x NTM).

model_inputs.structure_note: Driver-led quarterly set (16 quarters, 7 reported). Revenue = average paid memberships x subscription ARM x 3 + advertising revenue; operating income = revenue - cost of revenues (content amortization) - operating expenses. The value rests on one leg, a P/E horizon multiple (16.59x) on the model's own NTM GAAP EPS at 2027-11-17. Netflix is Communication Services and not on the FCF-leg list, so there is no FCF yield leg, and policy allows no DCF. The 2025-26 membership and ad-revenue quarter splits are estimates because Netflix stopped reporting memberships in 2025. ARM in the reported quarters is the residual that ties revenue to the filings.
model_inputs.gap_note: For Kilian: (1) this driver set (members, arm, ad_rev, cor, opex) is new and has not been approved on a card; the brief bars hearthbot calls here, so the supervisor should card it. (2) Judgment calls sized with model_engine.py on copies of this set (base 69.32). Over 5%: cost of revenues +10%/yr -7.7% (64.00); ARM +2%/yr -6.3% (64.95); ARM +4.5%/yr +6.6% (73.89); members adds halved -6.2% (65.00); ads -25% -6.1% (65.10); exit P/E at DIS 15.5x -6.6%. Under 5%: opex +9%/yr -4.0%; buybacks $8B/yr -1.7%; the run's 16.83x exit +1.5%. judgment_check.py was not run. (3) Peer set is 3 whole-company names (peer_count_flag) and the median rests on SONY, a borderline peer. (4) A buyback slowdown or a large sports-rights or M&A bid is below 20% probability and not modelled as a financing event.

comps_summary.peer_range: 15.5x (DIS) to 38.86x (SPOT) NTM P/E; META 18.6x and GOOGL 18.1x shown as segment-only
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 16.59x exit vs 17.66x whole-company median; own NTM 16.33x (peers.md)
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: No premium argued: the k = 0.8 shrink keeps most of today's small discount. The engagement data does not support a return to the old growth premium in the base case. Netflix's +18% FY2028 EPS growth (consensus 4.43 vs 3.74, src 9) against DIS +8% argues against a deeper discount, so the multiple stays inside the peer range.
comps_summary.peer_count_flag: 3 whole-company peers. Few listed companies run subscription video at scale: WBD is being bought by Paramount and PSKY is mid-merger (both distorted), ROKU is a platform and hardware business with thin earnings, CMCSA is cable-led, and Chinese peers (iQIYI, Tencent Video) are excluded by rule. META and GOOGL are shown as segment-only (advertising/attention) and kept out of the median.
